pts: Eliminate the hazard first; PPE is the last resort
Substitute: lower-risk chemical, prefab, lighter bags
Engineering: guards, LEV, edge rails, RCDs
Administrative: permits, procedures, rotation
PPE: only when the above are exhausted; wear it correctly
Falls are the top killer in construction worldwide
Use guardrails and covers before harnesses
Tie off 100% to a rated anchor, never to scaffold tubes
Inspect harness before each use; report any fall
Ladders are for access, not prolonged work
Stay out of swing/travel zones; eye contact with operator
Banksman for all reversing in congested areas
Walk on marked pedestrian routes
Hi-vis always; class 3 at night
Never ride on loads or in buckets
Every circuit through a 30 mA RCD; test weekly
Damaged cable = tag out and report
Keep plant and ladders away from overhead lines
Never touch a victim in contact with live electricity — isolate first
Only licensed electricians connect to DBs
One cubic metre of soil weighs about 1.5–2 tonnes
No entry > 1.5 m without shoring/sloping/box
Spoil and plant at least 1 m from the edge
Ladder every 7.5 m; inspect daily and after rain
Treat every underground cable as live
Permit first; clear combustibles 11 m
Fire watch with extinguisher during and 30–60 min after
Gas test for 0% LEL near process/tanks
Flashback arrestors on both ends; acetylene ≤ 1 bar
Know the nearest extinguisher, exit and assembly point
Never enter without permit, gas test and attendant
Isolate by blinding, not by closing valves
Rescuers die too — never enter to rescue without SCBA and retrieval
Evacuate on alarm or dizziness
Isolate every energy source, not just the stop button
One person, one lock, one key
Test for dead with a proved tester
Release stored energy: pressure, springs, raised parts
Only you remove your lock
Drink 250 ml every 15–20 min, before you feel thirsty
Rest in shade; heavy work early/late
New workers need 5–7 days to acclimatise
Confusion/no sweating = heat stroke: cool first, call 108
Look out for your buddy
Use plant or trolleys; split loads
Max 25 kg single-person; team lift above
Plan the route; bend knees; keep load close; no twisting
Report pain early
Cement bags: wear gloves; wash skin
Green tag only; red tag means do not use
Full boards, guardrails, toe boards, ties
Never remove a tie or brace
Use the ladder access, not the frames
Report any damage or missing part
Lift plan and signaller for every lift
Never stand under a load
Tag lines to control swing
Watch overhead lines: 3 m LT / 6 m HT clearance
Stop if the LMI alarms or wind rises
Read the label and SDS sections 2, 7, 8 before use
Right gloves and goggles for the chemical
Never mix; store incompatibles apart
Spill: isolate, PPE, contain, report
Wash before eating; no food in work areas
Dry cutting concrete/stone releases silica — use water or LEV
FFP3/P100 respirator for silica; fit-tested, clean-shaven
Silicosis is incurable; it appears years later
No dry sweeping; vacuum or wet
Change out of dusty clothes before going home
If you must shout at 1 m, protection is needed
Hearing loss is permanent and painless
Plugs/muffs in marked zones; fit them properly
Maintain silencers and enclosures
Attend your annual hearing test
Helmet with chin strap at height; boots; hi-vis — always
Inspect PPE daily; replace damaged free of charge
Right PPE for the task: goggles vs face shield vs welding helmet
Respirator fit: no beards for tight-fit masks
PPE never replaces a guard or a permit
Clean as you go; trips are the most common injury
Nails out of timber; tie wire in bins
Keep walkways and exits clear
Segregate waste; no burning
Store materials stable, not above 1.5 m by hand
Know the alarm sound and your assembly point
Raise alarm first, fight fire only if trained and safe
Call 112 / 101 / 108; give location and nature
Never use lifts in fire
Head-count: tell your supervisor you are out
Every near miss is a free lesson
No blame for reporting
Report within the shift to supervisor
Fix the cause, not the person
Celebrate the reports, trend them monthly
Inspect excavations and scaffolds after every rain
Lightning: stop WAH and crane work
Keep electrical DBs covered and cables raised
Slips: clean mud, use grip boots
Dengue/malaria: no stagnant water on site
Zero tolerance for harassment; ICC contact displayed
Night work: transport and security are your right
Report concerns confidentially
Separate facilities must be clean and lockable
Everyone shares responsibility for a respectful site
Assume every line is live
Keep tippers, booms, scaffold tubes and ladders well clear
Use goal posts and a spotter
If contact occurs: stay in the cab, jump clear only if on fire — keep others away
Ask for a shutdown or shrouding

t: Molten Metal – Water Is the Enemy
pts: Any moisture in charge, ladle or floor can cause a steam explosion
Preheat ladles; keep floors dry; never put water near a pour
Nobody in the pour route except the crew
Aluminised clothing, face shield, spats, metatarsal boots
Burn: cool with running water 20 min, go to OHC
Trucks stay in aisles; people stay on walkways
Make eye contact before crossing a truck's path
Forks low, horn at corners, seat belt on
Never stand under or ride on a raised load
Report racking impacts the same day

t: Lifting Gear – Check Before You Rig
pts: ID tag, WLL and this quarter's colour — no tag, no lift
Look for broken wires, stretch, cracks, cuts
Sling angle matters: wider angle, less capacity
Hook latch closed; shackle pin seated; never side-load
Damaged gear: tag it, hand it in, it gets destroyed
Guard on, correct disc, RPM rating checked
Cutting disc cuts; grinding disc grinds — never swap
Two hands, side handle, let it stop before putting down
Face shield plus glasses; FR clothing for sparks
Damaged cable or disc = tag out
Blind the lines — a closed valve is not isolation
Test the air at top, middle and bottom
Attendant stays; rescue gear rigged before entry
Pyrophoric scale: keep it wet
Any alarm or odour change: everybody out
A dust layer you can write your name in can explode
Vacuum, never blow down with air
Report sparks, hot bearings, smouldering immediately
No hot work until the area is cleaned and the process stopped
Keep Ex covers and seals closed
Escape respirator on you at all times in the area
Alarm sounds: move upwind/crosswind to the assembly point
Only the ERT with SCBA approaches a leak
Never spray water on a chlorine cylinder leak
Know the shelter-in-place room
Hydrogen builds up where batteries charge — no sparks, ventilate
Solar strings are live whenever there is daylight
Isolate DC and AC before touching connectors
Swollen or hot Li-ion cell: evacuate, isolate, call ERT
Rooftop PV work is work at height
Never walk or work under a load
Only the signaller talks to the operator
Tag lines on every load
Stop lifting when the anemometer says so
After a storm, no lifts until the crane is inspected
Three long sirens: clear the zone and go to the shelter
Sentries report clear before firing
After the blast, only the shot-firer goes in first
See a misfire or loose explosive? Don't touch, report
Hand back every cartridge and detonator
Hot bitumen is 150–180 °C — splash means deep burns
Water into hot bitumen = eruption
Face shield, gauntlets, long sleeves, heat-resistant boots
Burn: cool with water 20 minutes, leave bitumen on skin, go to hospital
Earth the tanker before transfer
Lifejacket on and clipped within 2 m of the edge
Know where the lifebuoy and rescue boat are
No jumping between vessels; use the gangway
Watch the tide and the sky
Man overboard: throw, shout, keep eyes on them
Fuel and power you log becomes our Scope 1 and 2
Refrigerant top-ups are emissions — record every kg
Idling plant burns money and carbon
Segregated waste can be recycled — that is EPR
Accurate meters today keep auditors happy tomorrow
Working without a permit or after it expires
Removing or bypassing guards and alarms
Not tying off at height; tying to scaffold tubes
Standing under loads or in the swing radius
Using damaged tools, cables or slings
Shortcuts: jumping, climbing frames, riding hoists
Phone use while operating plant or driving
Hot work without fire watch and clearing combustibles
Entering trenches or confined spaces without protection
Not reporting hazards and near misses — report them today
Missing guardrail or hole cover
Trench without shoring; spoil at the edge
Damaged cable; open DB; no RCD
Blocked exit; empty extinguisher
Leaking drum; unlabelled container
Unsecured cylinder; combustibles near hot work
Expired crane certificate; damaged sling
Poor lighting; slippery floor
If you see it — fix it, barricade it, or report it
Valid permit before high-risk work
Never bypass safety controls
Isolate and test before you touch
Confined space: permit, gas test, attendant
Protect yourself from falls
Plan every lift; stay out of the load path
Keep out of the line of fire
Drive safely; fit for work; right PPE
Stop unsafe work and report

t: First Aid – What Everyone Should Know
pts: DRSABCD: danger first, then response, then call 108
Not breathing: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, 100–120/min; get the AED
Severe bleeding: press hard and keep pressing
Burns: cool running water for 20 minutes; nothing else on it
Snake bite: keep still, splint, hospital — no tourniquet, no cutting
Chemical in eye: flush 20 minutes and go to hospital
Know your first-aider, the box location and the ambulance plan

t: Press Shop – Hands Out of the Die
pts: Test the light curtain and two-hand controls every shift — no test, no run
Never reach in to clear a misfeed: stop, isolate, then clear
Die setting only with safety blocks in and the press locked out
A double stroke is a near miss — report it the same shift
No bypass keys, taped sensors or foot pedals without guards
Ear plugs in; gloves off near rotating parts

t: Robot Cells – Nobody Inside While Live
pts: A still robot is not a safe robot — it may be waiting for a signal
Request entry, wait for the protective stop, take the gate key with you
Inside the cell carry the pendant with e-stop; stay out of pinch zones
Teach at reduced speed with the enabling device; second person at e-stop
Last person out sweeps the cell before reset — nobody restarts from outside blind
Any bypassed interlock is a stop-work
Thinner vapour needs only a spark: earth every container, no phones, no non-Ex tools
Ventilation on before you spray; airflow alarm means stop
2K clear coat = isocyanates = asthma for life; supplied air or PAPR, nobody else in the booth
Rags into self-closing metal bins; empty each shift
Never light an oven by hand; purge and flame-failure protect you
Hot work in the paint shop only with a permit and gas test

t: Weld Fume Is Not Just Smoke
pts: Welding fume is a Group 1 carcinogen — every indoor weld needs extraction
Keep the extraction nozzle close to the arc; if you can see fume in your face, it is not working
Galvanised sheet gives metal fume fever: chills after shift — report it
Stainless means hexavalent chromium — extraction plus RPE
Spot-weld tips crush fingers: both hands on the initiation, tips cool before dressing
Pacemaker wearers stay away from RSW transformers
Orange cables carry 400–800 V DC — only HV-authorised persons, never alone
Pull the service plug, wait the discharge time, prove the meter, test, then touch
Insulated tools, Class 0 gloves, face shield — no rings or watches
A swollen, hot or hissing cell leaves the building now
Lithium fires need huge volumes of water and come back for hours — call the fire service early
Damaged packs sit outside, 15 m away, watched with a thermal camera
No entry without the controller's clearance; radio on at all times
Know the speed band for your certification — limit tests only on the dynamic pad
Pull to the shoulder for any fault; never stop on the racing line
Pedestrians and maintenance only when the zone is closed
Rain, fog, lightning or dust: high-speed runs stop
Helmet and harness for limit-handling and rollover tests
Ammonia smells long before it hurts — any smell is a leak, leave and report
Escape respirator on your belt in every NH3 area
Oil draining: two people, dead-man valve, never walk away from an open drain
Never trap liquid between two closed valves
Water fog knocks down vapour; never spray liquid ammonia pools
Eyes or skin splashed: flush 20 minutes, then OHC
Acid plus bleach makes chlorine gas — one chemical at a time, rinse between
Add concentrate to water, never water to concentrate
Label every bottle; never use a drink bottle
Goggles and face shield for caustic — a splash in the eye is permanent
Before CIP starts, confirm nobody is inside the tank — lock the manway
Eyewash within 10 seconds: know where it is before you need it

t: Grain & Sugar Silos – Never Walk the Pile
pts: Flowing grain buries you knee-deep in 4 seconds and fully in 20
Clear bridges and walls from outside with poles — entry is the last option
Entry only with feeders locked out, atmosphere tested, lifeline and attendant
Never stand below hanging material
Dust layers explode: clean daily, no compressed-air blow-down, no hot work
If someone goes under, do not jump in — call rescue
Gas smell: stop, ventilate, isolate — never light by hand
Gauntlets and sleeves at ovens; open steam ovens from the side
Wet product into hot oil spits and boils over — dry it first
Fryer fire: lid or suppression, isolate heat, never water
Mixers and dividers: stop and isolate before scraping or clearing
Flour dust causes baker's asthma — tip under extraction, vacuum, no brooms
Hands never go into a running machine — stop, wait for run-down, use a tool
Glass bursts at the filler: face shield in the glass zone, tongs for shards
CO2 has no smell and fills low places — detector alarm means leave
Caustic from the bottle washer: goggles, gloves, isolate before cleaning
Palletiser cell: enter only through the interlocked gate with the key in your pocket
Wet floors: non-slip boots, clean spills now

t: Cold Room – Never Alone, Never Locked In
pts: Check the inside release before the door closes behind you
Sign in, carry a radio or alarm pendant, keep to the work/warm-up times
Shivering, numb fingers or confusion: leave now
CA rooms have 1–3 % oxygen — never enter to fetch fruit or a friend
Forklifts crawl inside: lights on, horn at doors, stop in fog
Frostbite: warm slowly, no rubbing
Vapour travels along the floor to the nearest spark
Earth the drum, the pump and yourself before pouring
No splash filling — dip pipe, slow start
Ex equipment only; a phone in Zone 1 is a bomb in your pocket
Peroxide-formers: test before you distil, never to dryness
Spent solvent: closed earthed drum, labelled, out within 90 days

t: Potent Compounds – Gown Right, Degown Slower
pts: Micrograms matter: no open handling of OEB 5 material
Glove ports and split valves are the containment — a torn glove is an incident
Degowning is where most exposure happens — slow, inside-out, respirator last
Wet clean only; no brooms, no compressed air
Pressure alarm or HEPA alarm: stop and report
Tell OHC early if you are pregnant or planning — hormones and cytotoxics are not negotiable

t: Clean-Room Work – Interlocks, Fumigation & Gas Suppression
pts: AHU work: isolate at the panel and the local switch, prove the fan is stopped
Door interlocks must release on the fire alarm — test the override
Fumigation in progress: locked, placarded, no entry until readings clear
Gas suppression room: isolate the release before maintenance inside; pre-discharge alarm means leave now
Nitrogen areas: watch the O2 monitor
Evacuate gowned — nobody degowns in a fire
Powder into solvent vapour through an open manway is how pharma fires start
Inert first: O2 below the limit on the analyser, purge on during charging
Earth the drum, the chute, the reactor and yourself; no plastic scoops or liners
Add at the planned rate and in the planned order — accumulation becomes a runaway
Temperature off profile: stop the feed, maximum cooling, call the shift in-charge
Never open a hot or pressurised vessel
Tight chest on Mondays is byssinosis starting — tell the OHC
Suction hoods and the filter plant are your lungs' protection — report blockages
No compressed-air cleaning while people are in the shed
Respirator for blow room, card stripping and waste rooms
Spirometry before and after the Monday shift — do not skip it
No smoking anywhere in the mill
Hydrosulphite plus moisture heats up and burns — keep drums sealed and dry
Peroxide away from reducers; acid away from bleach and caustic
Dye powders only in the booth with extraction and a mask
HT machine door opens only below 80 °C and zero pressure — never bypass the interlock
Steam valves open slowly; lagging stays on
Shower and eyewash: 10 seconds away, tested every week

t: Carding & Ring Frames – Stop Before You Clear
pts: Beater lids open only after the rotor has stopped — the timer is there for a reason
Card stripping with the machine stopped and locked
Hair covered, dupatta tucked, no loose sleeves — frames do not let go
Piece only where you were trained; stop for lapping and tape changes
Shuttle guards stay on; stop the loom before reaching in
Keep aisles and exits clear of trolleys
Wet-bulb above the limit: humidification off, ventilation on
Drink before you are thirsty; ORS in the summer
Dizziness, cramps, no sweating: cool area, water, tell the supervisor
New workers take 7–14 days to acclimatise — watch them
Air-washer tanks are confined spaces
Report hygrometer readings honestly — they protect you
Test the front gate every shift — the machine must not close with it open
Hands in the mould area only through the front gate, never rear or top
Stuck part: set-up mode, clamp blocked, tools not fingers
Mould change: inspected eyebolt, rated crane, hands never between the halves
Granulator blockage: stop, isolate, wait, then clear
Smoke from the barrel means decomposition — lower heat, ventilate
Purge behind the shield, face shield on, nobody in front of the nozzle
Hot plastic traps gas and spits — short shots into a metal tray
Never put a torch on a blocked die
Rupture disc in place or no start
PVC and POM fumes burn your lungs — extraction on
Hot screws and dies go in the marked cooling area

t: Two-Roll Mills – The Trip Bar Is Your Life
pts: Test the trip bar at the start of every shift — rolls must stop and separate
Two people on a running mill, always
No gloves, no loose sleeves at the nip
Feed with tools from above the guard line; cut with the knife away from the nip
Sticking stock: trip, stop, then clear
A near miss at the nip is reported the same hour
Ethyl acetate ignites at −4 °C — treat every tray as a fire waiting for a spark
Earthing straps and ionisers on before the web runs
LEL alarm: slow down, more exhaust, then stop
Dryer purge and flame safeguard never bypassed
Rags in closed bins; small quantities at the press
Blade changes with cut-resistant gloves and covers

t: Soldering Fume & Lead – Wash Before You Eat
pts: Rosin fume causes asthma — tip extraction on, nozzle close to the joint
Lead gets in through your hands: wash before breaks, no food at the bench
Skim dross with tools and a face shield, into a metal tin
Wet boards into the wave pot explode
Blood-lead tests are for you — attend them
Wheeze or chest tightness at work: report it
HF does not hurt at first — the burn goes to the bone hours later
Any skin contact: flush 5 minutes, rub in calcium gluconate gel, go to hospital
Double gloves, face shield, apron at the wet bench
Piranha: acid first, slow peroxide, never a closed container
TMAH through the skin can stop your breathing — flush and hospital even if you feel fine
Gas alarm: leave the zone, let the ERT handle it

t: Lithium Cells – Signs of Thermal Runaway
pts: Hissing, sweet smell, bulging, heat or smoke: move away and raise the alarm
Store at 30–50 % charge, cool, with aisles clear
Damaged or returned cells go to the outdoor quarantine, never back on the rack
Water in large volume cools; small extinguishers do not stop runaway
Fires re-ignite for days — thermal camera watch after any event
No metal tools or jewellery near terminals

t: Climbing the Tower – Clip, Check, Climb
pts: Two people, weather checked, control informed — then climb
Arrester on the rail before your foot is on the rung
Twin lanyards at every hatch: one on before one off
Close every hatch behind you; tools tethered
Rest at platforms; water every 30 minutes in summer
Dizzy or unwell: say so and come down
A person hanging in a harness can die within minutes — the team on the turbine is the rescue
Rescue kit at the top, rope long enough for the hub height, inspected monthly
Use the trauma straps if you are suspended; keep your legs moving
Lower the casualty, do not try to lift them up the ladder
Nacelle fire: personal descender, out through the hatch
Drill every six months — practice is the plan
All lock pins in, indicator and eyes agree, tag on — then open the hub hatch
Isolate pitch, converter and UPS; prove dead on every circuit
Accumulators at zero before touching hydraulics
Two in the hub or at the hatch, radio on
Wind over the limit or lightning alert: pins stay in, you come down
Hydraulic torque tools: hands clear of the reaction arm
Rope access only below the wind limit, dry, no lightning within range
Blade at 6 o'clock, rotor and pitch locked, recorded
Two ropes, two anchors, edge protectors — no exceptions
Grinding fibreglass: extraction and FFP3; resin on skin becomes an allergy
Spotter on the ground watches the sky and the road
Lightning alert: finish nothing, come off the blade

t: Lightning – 30 km Out, We Come Down
pts: Lightning at 30 km: pack up; at 15 km or thunder heard: leave the turbine or roof
Shelter in vehicles or the control building — never under the tower or a tree
Wait 30 minutes after the last strike before climbing again
Do not touch towers, fences or cables during a storm
After a strike on a turbine, inspect the lightning protection before work
The control room's call to descend is not a suggestion

t: Remote Site – Know Your Way to Hospital
pts: Ambulance is an hour away — the first aider on your crew is the first hour
Every vehicle has the turbine GPS list, the hospital route and an AED or knows where one is
Check in every hour; nobody works alone on HT, height or in confined spaces
Snakebite: still limb, pressure bandage, hospital with anti-venom — no cutting, no tourniquet
Heat stroke: cool first, drive second
Road accidents kill more technicians than turbines — seat belts, speed limits, no tired driving

t: Solar DC Is Live in Daylight
pts: Strings cannot be switched off while the sun is up — treat every DC cable as live
Open AC, open DC isolators, wait for discharge, prove the meter, test
Never pull a connector under load — check current first or cover the modules
Burnt or mismatched connectors start fires; replace, do not tape
Rain or lightning: no open enclosures
Fire service must be told DC stays live — nobody cuts cables
Cement sheets and skylights do not hold a person — walk only on boards over purlins
Clip to the lifeline before you leave the ladder
Rooflights covered or netted before anyone steps on the roof
Modules catch wind like sails: two people, stop at the wind limit
Never cut or drill asbestos sheets dry
A ten-minute cleaning job needs the same protection as installation
Gas alarm: doors stay shut — opening them can trigger an explosion
Move to the standoff distance and isolate remotely
Call the fire service with the chemistry and kWh — the ERP is in the control room
Water cools neighbours; nobody enters until gas and temperature are stable for a day
DC racks: isolate, wait, prove dead, insulated tools
Firmware and layout changes go through MoC
Nobody walks under a crane load or in the operational lane
Lashing from platforms and cages — never climb stacks
Twistlock indicators: locked before the lift
Rods in pairs, bins for twistlocks, gloves on
Wind rising: top tiers stop first, cranes stow at the limit
ITV drivers stay in the cab under the crane
Coal, grain, logs and steel eat oxygen; fumigated cargo leaves phosphine behind
No entry on smell or guesswork — a calibrated meter at three depths, then a permit
Attendant at the hatch never enters; rescuers wear SCBA or stay out
One person on the ladder at a time, tools on the hoist line
Grab or dozer working: nobody in the hold
Headache or dizziness: get out and report
The whole mooring deck and quay area is a snap-back zone
Never stand in a bight or in line with a tensioned line
Grab a line only when it is slack and on the quay
Lifejacket within 2 m of the edge and on the boat
Creaking or strand breaks: warn the ship, step well back
Someone in the water: lifebuoy and boat — never jump in
Placards and the declaration must match — if not, the box goes to the hold area
Fumigated units: ventilate, test, then open
Crack the doors from the side and step back
Leak or heat: isolate upwind, identify the UN number, call the DG officer
Ammonium nitrate and explosives do not stay in the yard
No smoking, no phones in the DG yard
Cane yard traffic kills more than machines: marshals, one-way, drivers out of the bay
Never hand-feed the carrier or clear a choke while it runs
Centrifugal lid opens only when the basket has stopped
Bagasse heats itself — probe the stacks, keep fire breaks clear
Hot juice and lime: face shield, open valves from the side
New workers wear the new-worker colour — look out for them
Most mill explosions start in the bucket elevator — belt slip, hot bearing, dust
Keep dust off ledges and motors; vacuum, no compressed air
Magnets and destoners stop tramp metal sparks
Never walk on stored grain; bins are entered only under permit
Phosphine fumigation is for licensed people only — keep out of placarded areas
Lift bags with your legs and a partner

t: New Season, New Workers – Buddy Up
pts: No one works near machines, vehicles or heights before induction in their language
Every new worker has a buddy for two weeks and wears the new-worker colour
Ask, do not assume: show how, watch, then sign off
Age proof for everyone; no under-18s on hazardous jobs
Safe camps: water, toilets, LPG kept outside, fire extinguisher
Report unsafe conditions — nobody loses wages for speaking up

t: DG Room – It Can Start by Itself
pts: Mains fails, the DG starts — AMF off, battery off, fuse out before any work
Back-feed can electrocute the lineman down the street: never bypass the interlock
Exhaust at 400 °C; no rags, no diesel near the manifold
Basement DG rooms: CO detector on, nobody inside during runs
Fuel transfer: bonding, drip tray, stop at 90 %
Doors closed, ear protection inside the enclosure

t: Refrigerant Rooms – Air You Cannot Smell
pts: A refrigerant leak pushes out the oxygen — the detector is your nose
Alarm: leave, ventilate, close the door, isolate from outside
Pressure test with nitrogen only — never oxygen or air
Brazing a line with refrigerant inside makes phosgene — recover first, purge with nitrogen
Cylinders upright, shaded, capped
Venting refrigerant is illegal and wasteful — recover it

t: Lift Shafts – Never Open a Landing Door Blind
pts: Most lift deaths are falls into an empty shaft — confirm the car is there
No jumpers on door locks; remove them before you leave
Car-top work only in INSPECTION mode with the stop switch and a second person
Pit entry with the car blocked and the stop switch on
Trapped passengers: trained mechanic releases, car at the landing, power off
Tell passengers to stay inside — climbing out between floors kills
Toilet acid plus bleach makes chlorine — never together
Labelled bottles only; gloves and goggles for toilet cleaning
Needles only in the puncture-proof box; never push waste down with hands
Needlestick: wash, report, PEP within 2 hours
No ladders above 3 m; façade work for trained people with harness
Nobody enters a septic tank or drain — ever
Count people in; stop at capacity — no free-entry rumours
Every exit unlocked, lit, staffed
Crowd surge signs: people falling, screaming, pressure — pause the show, open all exits
LED walls and trusses come down at the wind limit
Pandal fabric flame-retardant; LPG stalls separated; extinguishers everywhere
Medical post, AEDs and water points before the doors open

t: Sewer & Septic Tanks – No Manual Entry
pts: Manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks is illegal and lethal — machines do it
H2S kills in one breath and takes the rescuer next
Inspection entry only: isolate inflows, ventilate, test, lifeline, attendant, SCBA at the manhole
Attendant never enters; rescue is pulled out by winch
Rain forecast: no entry
Anyone asked to go in by hand says no and reports it
Berms at the edges, stop blocks at the tip, spotter at night
Light vehicles keep 50 m and call before overtaking
Reverse only with camera or spotter; pedestrians stay out of the pit road
Brakes tested on the grade every shift; seat belt on
Blocked crusher: isolate, release the energy from outside — no bars in a running jaw
Dust sprays on; mask when they are not
Hot meal is 800 °C powder that flows like water
Nobody stands below or in line with a poke hole or inspection door
Clear blockages remotely first; manual poking only in aluminised PPE from the side
Doors stay shut when meal is built up above
Restart flushes the kiln inlet — clear the area before feed on
Burn: cool with water 20 minutes, straight to hospital

t: CO – The Silent Killer in Steel Plants
pts: Blast-furnace gas has no smell; your CO monitor is the only warning
Monitor on, buddy with you, stay upwind of bleeders and stoves
Alarm: leave uphill and upwind, report — never finish the job
Collapsed colleague: do not go in without SCBA — call the rescue squad
Gas-line work only after goggle valve, blind, purge and test
Water near molten metal explodes — dry tools, dry charge
Nip points at every pulley — no cleaning near a running belt
Pull-cord tested, guards on, cross only at bridges
Coal dust on beams is explosion fuel — clean, no compressed air
Bunker CO rising means a fire inside: inert, do not open
Bunker and silo entry: isolate, test, lifeline, attendant
Ash is hot and flows — hopper poking under isolation only

t: Loading Dock – Chock Before You Load
pts: Trailer creeps, forklift drops — restraint or chocks and keys in the office first
Check the trailer floor and landing gear before driving in
Container doors open from the side with a strap
Loaders out of the trailer while the forklift is inside
Drivers wait in the driver room, not between vehicles
Green light means go; red means the trailer is not ready
Endothermic gas explodes if air gets in — never bypass the purge
CO monitor on in the furnace area
Low oil or hot oil: no quench — the load will light the tank
Water in oil or salt erupts; dry work, dry tools, dry salt
Fire in the tank: load stays under, lid down, suppression on, no water
Baskets with cracks do not go in the furnace
Earth the lorry before any hatch or hose
Engine off, chocks in, two people watching the whole decant
Right product, right tank — check the label twice
Phones, smoking, running engines: not on the forecourt
Spill: stop, isolate ignition, sand, report
Lightning: stop decanting
LPG sinks and travels — a leak at the carousel reaches the gate
Smell or alarm: stop, ESD, no ignition, move crosswind
Overfilled cylinder bursts in the sun — check-weigh every one
Jet fire: do not put it out until the gas is isolated; cool the tanks
Tank-lorry fire: 500 m back, BLEVE can happen
Earth, chock, engine off, hose in date — every lorry, every time
